Hey Diego,

Thanks again for the earlier demo. We have a technical validation scheduled next week and the eng team wants to run a full 48-hour throughput/latency benchmark against the endpoint to validate p95/p99 under production-ish traffic. High-level numbers:
- Target sustained RPS: 1,200 (burst to 3k for short periods)
- Avg prompt + completion size: ~450 tokens
- Goal: p99 < 200ms for served region (us-west), measure KV cache benefit

Can Redwood provide a safety-net promo (non-billable credits) or temporary quota bump so we can complete the run without early throttling? Rough ask: 200k token credits or equivalent ephemeral concurrency bump for 48h.

Attached: beta_poc_loadplan.csv, cost_projection_48h.pdf (rough estimate from our side).

We'd like to run 05/30 00:00 UTC — 05/31 00:00 UTC if possible. Please let me know what you need from our side (contact for run, additional test keys, SLA notes).

Cheers,

Diego — dug into their loadplan. A few technical notes:
- 1,200 RPS sustained with 450-token payloads is non-trivial; the main cost is token throughput + scheduling overhead.
- We can avoid a full Dedicated path if we provide a temporary concurrency bump + prefix cache hints. That should preserve representative latencies.
- My recommendation: approve a 40k token promo voucher plus a timeboxed concurrency window (50% higher concurrent slots) for a 12–24 hour peak segment of the run rather than full 48h. That reduces risk to capacity and protects other customers.

If Marissa signs off on the voucher, SE and I will schedule tuning (cache hints, model variant selection) and a live monitoring session during the run. We should also set an automated fallback to a cheaper quantized variant at 90% of allocated throughput.

Estimated internal cost and risk: ~40k tokens + 12h burst (low-medium). If Beta insists on full 48h unthrottled and 200k tokens, we should request cost-share or move them to a short-term Dedicated commitment.

-Karthik
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
